question: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is the maestro in playing the ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**sarod**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is an acclaimed Indian classical musician renowned for playing the **sarod**.
 
• He is considered one of the greatest sarod players and has significantly contributed to the popularity of this instrument globally.
 
• Amjad Ali Khan has been performing for over six decades, showcasing the rich heritage of Indian classical music.
 
• He has received numerous awards, including the Padma Vibhushan, one of India's highest civilian honors.
 
• His style is characterized by a deep, resonant tone and a profound understanding of ragas, the melodic frameworks in Indian classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarod**

 
 
• The sarod is a stringed instrument used mainly in Indian classical music.
 
• It is known for its deep, weighty, and introspective sound and is a prominent instrument in Hindustani classical music.
 
• The sarod has a fretless fingerboard, allowing for the continuous slides between notes that are characteristic of Indian music.
 
• It typically has 17 to 25 strings, including both playing and sympathetic strings.
 
 
 
• **Raga**
 
 
• A raga is a framework for melodic improvisation in Indian classical music, akin to a melodic mode in Western music.
 
• Each raga is associated with a specific mood, time of day, and season.
 
• Ragas are constructed using a specific set of notes and include characteristic motifs and ornamentations.
 
 
 
• **Padma Vibhushan**
 
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award in India.
 
• It is awarded for exceptional and distinguished service in any field, including arts, literature, science, and public services.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music**
 
 
• Indian classical music is divided into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian).
 
• It is characterized by the use of ragas (melodic modes) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
• Indian classical music places a strong emphasis on improvisation and exploration of a raga within the framework of a tala.
